questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Academic nuance and new ways of learning from new aspects, that the destination had a university with subjects I wanted to take, that it would contribute to my professional profile, that I found the country and its culture interesting and wanted to explore that.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The information was all there, but it was spread across so many different sources and hand-outs, that it was difficult to keep track of. Furthermore, the university sent wrong or outdated information a couple of times, which was okay, but confused the information-processing a bit.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received a lot the first days of university, and then I received a lot, when I learned where to ask for help.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was at a dormitory through the university, but it was 40 minutes off campus on foot.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Public transportation is good when you figure it out, and its pretty nice with walking except during rainy season or when it's super hot! Remember to buy an umbrella and take public when there's a heath wave warning.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The dormitory I lived at was fine, but very weird. Not that social and cleaning standards in the units were very bad (students cleaned common areas in the units themselves on a schedule, and very differing how well this was done).

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very confusing, but loads of guides to do so - just so many, that information became muddled.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Signed up for wished courses, and then again for which courses you would actually like when the registration opened. Then you got some assigned and some not, which led to a new process. It was all done through excel-sheets and email.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: OUSSEP has officies at the campus, which was very helpful!

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: 50/50. I got half of the ones I initially wanted, so if you really want them all, the chances are not that great. Make sure to scout out some more you would like.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do it! Very interesting and fun. Some classes were not that interesting and the learnings low, but others were super interesting, challenging and I learned a lot.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was super confusing! Some classes were very, very easy, to the point where it felt like a waste of time. Other classes were super hard, and demanded a lot(!) of preparation. I was very confused by the level being so different from course to course! A lot of reading for all of the classes, which was a little hard to manage since I had 8 different courses. The exam period was very hectic, but also taught me quite a lot.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Differed depending on the teacher. Some taught a lot like at UCPH, but others in a more seminar kind of manner, and others in a more discussion-forum kind of way.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: "Japan: Society and Ideology", "Peace and conflict Studies", "Sociological Analysis of Nihonjin-ron", "Food, Culture and Society", "Globalization Studies", "Ethics and criminology", "Issues in Gerontology" and "Seminar in Studies of Multicultural Societies"

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: "Globalization Studies" and "Ethics and criminology" (Both with the same teacher, who was an AMAZING teacher. I learned a lot and was a great classroom for discussion and reflection), "Peace and conflict Studies" (A REALLY interesting and important class where I learned a lot. However, the teacher was very strict, or mean, did make several students cry and the work load was very heavy), "Seminar in Studies of Multicultural Societies" (Sweet teacher, interesting subjects), "Sociological Analysis of Nihonjin-ron" (nice way to learn about non-western theories and methods in academia)

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had e-sim troubles, which made som unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Pre-made food and eating out was way less expensive than home cooking. Fresh fruit and vegetables was more expensive than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Really whatever you could dream about, all kinds of interests were represented.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Traveling to nearby cities. Visiting temples and shrines. Going to local culture festivals. Experiencing nightlife. Eating out a lot. Singing karaoke with friend-groups (a must do). Saying Yes to things.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on weekend-trips to other cities or go to Osaka to experience all it has to offer.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Relatively easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It was very difficult. It was made easier by living at a dormitory with local students, however many were uncomfortable with speaking english, so it was easier to do "stuff" together, instead of talking.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Humor, speaking English, cleaning-standards, and when its socially acceptable to make noise - it wasn't uncommon for my roomates to wash clothing or use the vacuum-cleaner in the middle of the night.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Food, nature, spirituality (as a non-spiritual person), art and architecture, culture-meetings, and so much more.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Its SUPER overwhelming (especially if you don't speak japanese), but it was also SUPER worth it!!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything is done through Line and prepare for a lot of paperwork!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Learning a lot of new things from totally different perspectives.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being away from my home, friends and family with so much time difference.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Thank you for the help and the possibility.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
